messages:
Elle: FYI CardiaHealth submitted their vendor security questionnaire and flagged two items blocking procurement: (1) they want SOC2 evidence and a list of subprocessors, (2) confirmation on our embeddings retention/pseudonymization approach for PHI. They said procurement will pause renewal unless we answer by EOD Friday.

Devin: Thanks Elle — can you paste the link to the vendor form and checklist? I can draft the evidence package.

Elle: Link: https://redwood.share/drive/cardia-vendor-q (viewer). Key ask from them: 'Do you store embeddings with tenant identifiers? How long are embeddings retained? Is PII pseudonymized before storage?' + 'Provide latest SOC2 report or SOC2 letter'.

Sanjay: @Devin I can pull SOC2 letter and subprocessors list. NOTE: SOC2 report is under NDA, we usually share a redacted copy and a signed NDA is required. For subprocessors I can produce a CSV (name, role, region). Also: for SGX/BYOK customers we have additional key provenance docs.

Devin: Great. For embeddings retention: default retention is 30 days for ephemeral indexing; for cust-managed datasets we persist per contract. For PHI customers we recommend private deployment + customer-managed KMS. We should state that pseudonymization is available via our transform pipeline (sample code snippet).

Maya: Example pseudonymization snippet I usually include:```
# pseudonymize before embedding
text = re.sub(r"\\b(\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4})\\b", "<SSN>", text)
embedding = client.embed(text)
store(embedding, metadata_without_identifiers)
```

Devin: Drafting a short-answer doc: 1) SOC2: redacted SOC2 Type II available after NDA — attach letter + contact. 2) Subprocessors: attached CSV. 3) Embeddings: default retention 30d, configurable by plan; pseudonymization is customer-level prior to ingestion OR we can enable transform in ingestion pipeline (not enabled by default). 4) For PHI: recommend Private deployment; we also support BYOK and KMIP integrations.

Elle: Procurement asked whether we can provide a signed DPA addendum. We have a template but legal needs to confirm any custom clauses. @Sanjay any issues with sharing DPA template?

Sanjay: We can share standard DPA + subprocessors list. For custom clauses (data residency + breach notification windows) might need legal review. I'll ping legal separately.

Onboarding Bot: Checklist update: vendor-form: received -> status: awaiting evidence package (owner: Devin). NDA required for SOC2: not sent. DPA requested: template available.

Devin: Action plan: 1) Send Cardia the DPA template + request NDA for SOC2 access. 2) Attach redacted SOC2 letter and subprocessors CSV. 3) Provide short FAQ about embeddings retention and pseudonymization (one-pager). I can assemble and send by EOD.

Elle: Thanks — please add a brief renewal-risk note for AMs: procurement will delay renewal if not resolved. I'll cc the AM in the outbound.

Devin: Will do. Quick Q: who should be on the call if Cardia asks for deeper technical walk-through? I'd propose @Sanjay + Solutions engineer (Maya) + me.

Maya: happy to join the call, can do a 30m deep-dive on ingestion transforms.

Sanjay: I can join for security questions.

Elle: Perfect. Devin — mark as owner and post the outbound message in thread when sent.

Devin: Will post the message here once I send it. Expect draft in ~2 hours. :thumbsup:
